chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from one of our companions, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Rabi' ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Suleym al-Aamiri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Isa ibn Maryam came to the grave of Yahya ibn Zakariyya (peace be upon them), and he had asked his Lord to revive him for him. So he called out to him, and he answered him and came out to him from the grave, and said to him, 'What do you want from me?' So he said to him, 'I want you to comfort me just as you used to in the world.' So he said to him, 'O Isa! The heat of death has not yet settled from me, and you want to return me to the world, and the heat of death to return upon me?' So he left him, and he returned to his grave.

key_terms.حَرَارَةُ الْمَوْتِ: Heat of death (a metaphor for the lingering effects or reality of death)

ai.seo_question: What happened when Isa asked for Yahya to be revived from his grave?
ai.summary: In this unique narrative from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) recounts Jesus visiting John the Baptist's grave to seek companionship, illustrating the profound bond between these prophets. John’s refusal to return permanently highlights the Shia theological distinction between the temporary 'minor resurrection' (Nushur al-Sughra) experienced by prophets and the final, permanent resurrection, noting that the 'heat of death' remains until the Day of Judgment.
